title: Homological Thresholds in Randomly Monitored Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
summary: Random projective measurements are an effective tool to model the interlinked phenomenology of monitoring, inferring, and decoding highly entangled states such as quantum error-correcting codes. At the same time, the study of such monitored dynamics has opened a new arena for critical phenomena, renewing longstanding questions in disordered statistical mechanics, including percolation, random-bond models, and Nishimori physics.
